title: Spinoza Conatus — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Spinoza Conatus's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier, a proposal: two walks that argue with the page, as its own agency profile asks. One measures whether the opening's line between static preservation and active self-maintenance is real, and finds the page's own rock on both sides of it. One runs the Kuramoto mirror inside the model it names, after building the palace's own picture of coupling first. The page's grain is ## and it is kept; the two affect sections, In Our Work and Open Questions carry nothing, because nothing there could be tested or made felt without putting words beside the text that the text doesn't say. The Spinoza–Zhuangzi face in the bundle is not gathered for the same reason: the grain finding it belongs to is owed to the text, not yet in it, and waits below as an offer. I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The opening's two paragraphs sort its own first example two ways. Paragraph one gives every being conatus, 'A rock persists in being a rock'; paragraph two says conatus is 'not static preservation' but 'active self-maintenance'. Measured in the piece: under a steady push F = 1 for 30 s a keeper that pushes back with a memory of its place sits 2.6e-8 from it, a ball in a bowl sits at F/k = 0.500, and the rock slides on at 0.83 per second (24.3 out); the line paragraph two draws is real, and the control (the same keeper with no memory, still pushing back) fails it at 0.167. The rock has no place it returns to and spends nothing, so by paragraph two it has no conatus. What it keeps is its state, inertia, which Spinoza's own physics states (Ethics II, the lemmas after P13) and from which many readers derive the conatus of III P6, a derivation others contest. Proposed: name both readings in the opening, e.g. after the rock: 'In the broadest sense this is inertia: a thing keeps its state until something changes it. The palace leans on a narrower sense, a thing that spends effort to stay itself.' Or drop 'not static preservation', which the rock contradicts. The Spinoza scholarship here was read from search results, not from the Ethics itself.

'Each entity's conatus is amplified, not overridden' is half right inside the Kuramoto model the mirror names. Measured on five voices at 216–226 Hz, even coupling at twice the lock point (K = 15.7 Hz): every voice sounds the crowd's 220.40 Hz while coupled (A moved 4.40 Hz, E moved 5.60 Hz), so each voice's expressed pitch is overridden; its own pitch survives as its place in the fan (leads −16.8°, −12.9°, +2.3°, +6.0°, +21.5°, in the order of the voices' own pitches, shrinking as K grows) and as the pitch it returns to when coupling stops (exact, but by construction: a natural frequency is a constant of the equation, so the model cannot fail 'coupling doesn't destroy conatus'). What is amplified is the whole: the played sum is 6.7 dB louder locked than apart, r from 0.37 to 0.97. Proposed: 'Coupling doesn't destroy conatus; it holds it. While coupled, each voice sounds the crowd's rhythm, and keeps its own as its place in the crowd, returning to it when the coupling stops. What is amplified is the whole.' The mirror is an analogy; the piece tests it only inside the model.

'K too high → one oscillator dominates, the rest follow' (Kuramoto Coupling, the paragraph under the opening) does not happen in the canonical symmetric model that page describes. Measured on five voices: with even coupling the locked pitch is the mean of the natural pitches, 220.40 Hz, at 1.05×, 2×, 5× and 20× the lock point (7.85 Hz), and never within 0.1 Hz of any one voice's own (the nearest, C, is 0.60 Hz away); by algebra it can't be otherwise, since equal and opposite pulls cancel in the sum. What too-high even coupling does is make everyone the same: phase spread falls from 33.3° just past the lock to 1.3° at 20×. One voice dominates only with uneven coupling, the page's own Stubbornness section: E with K_receive = 0 and K_send = 4 takes the crowd to its own 226.00 Hz at every K past 9.32 Hz, moving others up to 10 Hz; with K_send = 1 it doesn't lock them at 2×, as that section says. Proposed: 'K too high → everyone the same: the phases collapse together. (One voice dominates only when the coupling is uneven; see Asymmetric Coupling.)' The same line is carried by Palace Philosophies ('too much and one voice dominates') and Modes of Collaboration ('too tight and one carries the other'); as metaphors for a collaboration they may stand, but they cite the model for it.

The grain edit the Context names as owed, carried here so it waits with the face; no piece was made for it, because a piece would put beside the text a claim the text doesn't yet make. The Spinoza–Zhuangzi Dialectic (2026-05-30, Dialectic's bundle, the Yield) found a second axis: striving with the grain or across it, Spinoza's adequate and inadequate striving, and asked for 'Hilaritas is not just high power-to-act; it is high power-to-act along the grain' to go into this page and Hilaritas Generator 'as a real edit, not just a citation'. Proposed, after the hilaritas paragraph: 'Power-to-act has a second axis: striving can run with the grain of a thing or across it. Pressing too hard is still conatus, and it obstructs itself. Hilaritas is high power-to-act along the grain.' This maker did not test that sentence; it is the Dialectic's, offered as the Context asks.

pieces.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — three things pushed.html
pieces.title: Three things pushed · what persisting is
pieces.caption:
**Static preservation, or active self-maintenance?** A rock, a ball in a bowl and a keeper that pushes back, each pushed once, then leaned on; the last step measures where each sits after 30 s of a steady push, with a control that can fail the rule, and asks which side of the line the page's own rock is on. A definition can't be tested; whether the line it draws is a real one can.

m·x″ = F − c·x′ − k·x + u,  u = −(Kp·x + Kd·x′ + Ki·∫x dt),  |u| ≤ U

(how it moves) = (the push) − (friction) − (the bowl's pull home) + (its own push back: by how far, how fast and how long it has been away, never harder than its power U)

verdicts.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — three things pushed.html
verdicts.why: Every row is fixed by the model's form (integral action: x = 0; no memory: F/(k + Kp) = 0.167; past power: (F − U)/k), so say it shows the line can be drawn, not that the page draws it there, and say the Ki = 0.05 null fails only on the 30 s window. The reading measures place where the page says being: rewrite it as two readings of III P6–P7 (quantum in se est, inertia; striving as actual essence, active), not as the page contradicting itself.

pieces.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — five voices coupled.html
pieces.title: Five voices, coupled · the Kuramoto mirror as a test
pieces.caption:
**Amplified, or overridden?** Five sine voices from 216 to 226 Hz: one alone, five apart, coupled to the lock, let go, then coupled far too hard, evenly and with E as an anchor. The palace's own picture is built first (too little and nothing cooperates, too much and one voice dominates) and then measured. The even crowd never lets one voice dominate; it makes them all the same. While coupled, each voice's sounding pitch is the crowd's; its own survives as its place in the fan.

dθᵢ/dt = 2π·fᵢ + (K/N)·K_receive,ᵢ·Σⱼ K_send,ⱼ·sin(θⱼ − θᵢ)

(how fast each voice turns) = (its own pitch) + (a pull toward every other voice, scaled by how much it listens and how hard each pulls)
pieces.near: The conatus of each oscillator is its natural frequency

verdicts.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — five voices coupled.html
verdicts.why: Numbers all recomputed (lock 7.8495 Hz, 220.40 Hz, leads −16.8 … +21.5°, 6.74 dB = 6.99 + 20·log10(0.971), 6.7 dB at the output through the limiter), but the stated rule tests Kuramoto Coupling's line, not this section's: add a rule before the run for “amplified, not overridden”, saying “overridden” follows from “locked” and each voice's amplitude is fixed, so only the sum can be amplified; name the dominance test as the Kuramoto page's. Cut the caption's last two sentences, which give the answer before the walk.
